title: Degree-zero localization at a homogeneous prime is exact
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard], and let $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ be an exact sequence of $\mathbf Z$-graded $S$-modules with degree-preserving maps. For every homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ of $S$ not containing the irrelevant ideal $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], let $T$ be the multiplicative set of homogeneous elements of $S$ outside $\mathfrak p$. Write $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$ for the degree-zero subring of $T^{-1}S$: its elements are fractions $a/h$ with $a,h$ homogeneous, $h\in T$, and $\deg a=\deg h$. Write $M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ for the degree-zero $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$-submodule of $T^{-1}M$: its elements are fractions $y/h$ with $h\in T$, $y\in M$ homogeneous, and $\deg y=\deg h$, modulo the usual localization equivalence $y/h=y'/h'$ if some $t\in T$ satisfies $t(h'y-hy')=0$; likewise for $M'$ and $M''$. The maps on these modules are $y/h\mapsto\phi(y)/h$ for the two given graded maps $\phi$. Then $0\to M'_{(\mathfrak p)}\to M_{(\mathfrak p)}\to M''_{(\mathfrak p)}\to0$ is exact as a sequence of $S_{(\mathfrak p)}$-modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-localization-short-exact] to the given exact sequence and the multiplicative set T. This gives an exact sequence of ordinary localized modules 0 \to T^{-1}M' \to T^{-1}M \to T^{-1}M'' \to 0, with the displayed fraction maps.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00HT (algebra-lemma-flat-localization) and the exactness of localization

proof.text: Because T consists of homogeneous elements, each localized module has the induced Z-grading in which a homogeneous fraction y/h has degree deg(y)-deg(h), and the localized maps preserve this grading. The fraction formulas are compatible with the localization relation, so this is well defined.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00JL (section-graded-modules), localization of graded modules at homogeneous elements

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-degree-component-exact] to the induced graded exact sequence in Step 2 at degree zero. Its degree-zero terms are exactly the submodules M'_(p), M_(p), and M''_(p), since degree zero means that the homogeneous numerator and denominator have equal degree. Under these identifications the maps are y/h \to phi(y)/h, so the resulting sequence is the one asserted.
